"A short rewarding night, minutes"
The coordination meeting began on time

Attendees were Tomas Garcia, Grace Garcia, Milolet, and the shift desk team.

The team reviewed the steady flow of passenger requests across Aurelia Skyways and confirmed that companion animal bookings need calm handling from first contact to handoff. I stressed that every reply must stay clear and brief, because confused instructions slow the desk and increase stress for travelers and animals alike. The group agreed that the strongest support comes from consistent checks on carrier readiness, document review, and direct coordination with the cabin team before boarding begins.

We also discussed a few recent cases where travelers arrived anxious and needed extra reassurance. In those moments, the desk must keep its tone even and humane, and handlers should avoid rushed movements around the animals. The team noted that Milolet remained settled during the review, which helped reinforce the value of quiet handling and simple routines. Grace Garcia and Tomas Garcia were mentioned in the context of smooth communication, and the group agreed that clear expectations at the desk reduce last-minute pressure.

Attention then shifted to in-flight monitoring. The cabin team is expected to keep watch on animal comfort without disturbing nearby passengers, and any change in behavior must be relayed quickly to the desk. The shift coordinator reminded everyone that small signs of distress matter and should not be ignored. The team also agreed to keep records current so the next shift can pick up each case without delay or guesswork.

The meeting closed with a short review of open tasks, including document checks, follow-up calls, and readiness for the next wave of passengers moving through Aurelia Skyways. Everyone was reminded to stay alert, keep communication direct, and preserve a calm working pace throughout the remainder of the shift.
